get.summary: `GET /api/canvas?path=<path>` — read and validate a canvas document.
get.description:
Returns `{ canvas, rejected, kiln }`. Any node whose reference fails
containment is **redacted in the returned canvas** — a `file` node loses its
path, a `group` loses its background — and described in `rejected` so the UI
can render a quarantined placeholder explaining why.

This is the fail-safe layer. A `.canvas` hand-edited on disk to point at
`../../../etc/passwd` reaches this handler like any other, and the offending
path never leaves the process.

The body schema describes one SSE `data:` payload, not the whole stream:

get.summary:
`GET /api/notes/resolve?kiln=<path>&name=<target>` — resolve a wikilink
target to a file, **by walking the kiln**.
get.description:
Deliberately independent of the note index. Opening `[[Some Note]]` is a
path question, and answering it from the index means a kiln that has not
been processed yet resolves nothing — which does not fail loudly, it falls
through to whatever kiln is configured as the default and silently opens a
same-named note from the wrong vault. Indexing is an optimisation for search
and backlinks; it must not be a prerequisite for following a link.

Resolution order, matching how wikilinks are written in practice:
  1. exact kiln-relative path (with or without the `.md` suffix)
  2. unique filename stem anywhere in the kiln

An ambiguous stem resolves to the shallowest match, which is the same
tie-break the link index applies.

# Isolation

**A root never resolves outside itself.** Every candidate is canonicalized
and checked against the canonical root, so a symlink planted inside one kiln
cannot surface a note from another kiln or from a project. Resolution
failing is the correct outcome — the alternative, quietly answering from a
different root, is how a link in one vault silently opens a same-named note
from another.

post.summary: `POST /api/plugins/command` — invoke a plugin command by name.
post.description:
Not under `/{name}` because a command's name is already globally unique —
the daemon refuses a second plugin claiming one — so routing by plugin would
ask the caller for something it does not need to know. The result is passed
through verbatim, like publications and options: what a command returns is
the plugin's vocabulary, and a shape this layer validated would be a shape
only today's plugins could send.

get.summary: `GET /api/plugins/commands` — the executable primitives plugins declared.
get.description:
Each entry carries `plugin`, `name`, `description`, `hint`, `parameters`
and `effect`. The names are read, so the browser is told what a row holds;
`parameters` is passed through verbatim, so a caller offering a command as
a button — with a dialog built from the declared parameters — needs no
change on this side when a plugin ships a new one.

`parameters` crosses as opaque JSON today. It comes from the same
`ToolDefinition` a tool uses, so shaping it like `signature.rs`'s JSON
Schema output is what would let a dialog be generated rather than
hand-read — see `docs/Meta/Analysis/The Plugin Contract.md`.

get.summary: `GET /api/plugins/events` — a push when a plugin's published data changes.
get.description:
The counterpart to `GET /api/plugins/publications`: that answers "what is
true now", this says "read it again". A panel drawing a plugin's own state
would otherwise poll on a timer and still show a stale value between ticks.

Same shape as the file-tree stream in `routes/fs.rs`, including the
load-bearing ordering: subscribe the LOCAL broker channel before telling the
daemon to forward, because `EventBroker::dispatch` drops events for a
session id with no local subscriber and the window between the two calls
would lose the first event.

post.description:
The client sends a `{}` body this handler never reads, and that is
deliberate — see the note on `resolveReviewComment` in `review-api.ts`.
The empty object forces `Content-Type: application/json`, which puts the
request outside the CORS simple-request set and makes the browser preflight
it against an allowlist that refuses cross-origin callers. It is the second
layer behind the `SameSite=Strict` auth cookie, not a redundant one: an
"optimisation" that drops the body drops the header, and every review write
becomes something a foreign page can fire blind.

AgentListResponse.description:
The agent picker's list.

The key is `agents`, where the daemon's own answer says `profiles`: this
route names the list after what the picker shows, and the ROW is the
daemon's, so a probed field cannot be dropped on the way through.

AgentOptionChoiceRow.description: One choice in an agent's select option.

value.description: The value to send back when this choice is picked.

name.description: What to show for it.

oneOf.description: Pick one of several values.

current.description: The value the agent reports as current.

choices.description: Every value it accepts, in the order it listed them.

oneOf.description: On or off.

current.description: The value the agent reports as current.

AgentOptionKindRow.description:
The control an agent option asks for.

A tagged union rather than a `kind` string beside a loose `current`: a
select carries choices and a string, a toggle carries a bool, and the
browser's hand-written type declared `current: string | boolean` with
optional choices because nothing described the pairing.

allOf.description: The control to draw, and its current value.

id.description: The id to name when setting the option.

name.description: What to label the control.

description.description:
Help text the agent supplied, or `null`. Always written, so
`required` rather than optional.

category.description: The agent's own category string, or `null`. Presentation only.

AgentOptionRow.description: One setting an external agent advertised for itself.

options.description:
Empty until the first message, and empty for an internal agent always:
an agent advertises nothing until the daemon connects to it.

AgentProfileEntry.description: One ACP agent profile, with the availability probe's verdict.

description.description: The profile's description, or an empty string when it declares none.

command.description:
The command that spawns the agent, or an empty string when the profile
names none. A profile with no command can never spawn, so it is never
available.

is_builtin.description: Whether the daemon ships this profile, rather than a config declaring it.

available.description: Whether the probe found the command on PATH and it answered `--version`.

AnchoredEdit.description: One change: the text expected, and what replaces it.

expect.description: The text this edit expects to find. Matched against WHOLE LINES.

replace.description: What replaces it. May carry newlines, so one line becomes several.

occurrence.description:
Which match to take when `expect` legitimately appears more than once,
zero-based. Absent means the text must appear exactly once.

ArchiveResponse.description: Response for session archive/unarchive status changes.

BacklinkRow.description: A note whose wikilinks point at the focused note.

path.description: Kiln-relative, as the index holds it.

title.description: `null` when the source note declares no title. Always written.

abs_path.description:
The same source joined onto the kiln root. Added by this route, not by
the daemon.

span_start.description:
Byte offset of the first link occurrence in the source. Absent — not
`null` — for a span-less legacy index row.

BlockRef.description: Where in a note a hit sits.

span_start.description: Byte offset where the block starts, relative to the note body.

span_end.description: Byte offset one past the block's last byte.

cited.description:
Further `(span_start, span_end)` pairs a `search:rerank` handler cited
for this hit, in the order it gave them. Empty for a plain block hit.

Canvas.description:
A parsed `.canvas` document.

Both arrays are optional in the spec; a canvas with neither is legal and
means "empty". Node order carries meaning — it *is* the z-order, first
lowest — so this is a `Vec`, never a set or map.

CanvasColor.description:
A canvas colour.

On the wire this is always a JSON string: either `#RRGGBB` or one of the six
presets `"1"`–`"6"`. Presets are numeric *strings*, not numbers, and writing
them back as numbers makes Obsidian stop recognising them — so this stays a
transparent newtype over the raw string rather than an enum that might
normalise the spelling.

CanvasEnd.description: Whether a connection terminates in an arrowhead.

CanvasNode.description:
The on-disk shape of a node: spec-common fields, the `type` tag, and one
undifferentiated bag for everything else.

This is also where the OpenAPI schema for a node comes from. [`Node`] reads
and writes JSON THROUGH this struct, so describing `Node`'s own fields would
describe a shape that never reaches the wire — `kind` and `extra` are not
keys any client sees. [`Node`]'s `ToSchema` therefore delegates here, and a
field added to this struct reaches the document without a second edit.

Field order here IS the emitted key order, and it is chosen to match what
Obsidian writes so that saving an untouched canvas produces no diff. The
type-specific keys live in `rest`, which is why they land between `type` and
the geometry for `file`/`text`/`link` — and why a group's `label`, which
Obsidian writes *after* the geometry, is re-inserted there on the way out.

canvas.description: The document, with every refused reference already removed.

rejected.description: One entry per reference the document held and this reply withholds.

kiln.description: The root the canvas belongs to, which bounds every reference in it.

CanvasSide.description: Which edge of a node a connection attaches to.

display.description:
The daemon's "which argument matters" projection, shared with the
TUI. `Value` because `ToolDisplay` lives in `crucible-core`, which
takes no utoipa dependency (same deal as `stop_reason` below).

auto_approved.description: Which layer granted permission without asking, if any.

diffs.description:
Proposed file edits as `FileDiff` objects (`{path, old_content,
new_content}`); `old_content: null` means a whole-file write. The
browser renders the card's diff from this instead of re-deriving
one from the tool name and arguments.

terminate.description:
True if this tool requested an agent-turn early-stop
(daemon's conjunctive batch-terminate check fired). UI renders
a "Terminated" badge on the tool card.

oneOf.description:
A text segment that streamed before a tool call, carrying the turn's
`message_id`, its 0-based `index`, and the segment text. Lets the
frontend materialize a canonical per-segment bubble that matches
history reconstruction.

stop_reason.description:
Why the turn ended (`end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `refusal`, …). The
browser reads it to style the turn. Absent when the daemon
reported none.

It is a `String` in the document because `StopReason` lives in
`crucible-core`, which takes no utoipa dependency. The values are
`StopReason::ALL`, serialised snake_case.

stop_notice.description:
The note the browser draws under a reply the provider cut off, or
absent when the reason needs none — which is every normal turn.

**The daemon words it, not the page.** `StopReason::user_notice`
is the only wording; the browser held a second one in TypeScript
and the two drifted. One `Option<String>` once per turn is cheaper
than a wording nothing compares, and `AGENTS.md` puts the decision
in the daemon for exactly this reason: a web front end must not
duplicate it.

ChatEvent.description:
The browser's view of a session event, streamed by `GET
/api/chat/events/{session_id}`.

`ToSchema` publishes the 21 tag values to the OpenAPI document, so the
browser reads the union from the enum instead of repeating it.

url.description: Remote repo: https://…, git@host:…, or `owner/repo` shorthand.

dest.description:
Where to put the clone. Absolute, and it must not exist. Absent takes
`[workspace] root_dir/<repo-name>`.

name.description: The project name for the clone. Absent takes the name in the URL.

CommandEffectRow.description:
Whether running a command changes state a user could lose, mirroring
[`crucible_lua::CommandEffect`].

**Declared by the plugin and verified by nothing.** A consumer must present
it as a claim, and a permission layer must treat it as a hint about what to
ask — never as permission to skip asking.

A closed set, not the open string a passthrough would give, because the
daemon writes `CommandEffect::as_str()` and nothing else: a command that
declares no effect arrives as `write`, never as an unknown word.
`the_mirrored_vocabularies_stay_closed` holds the two lists together.

CommandResponse.description:
What one slash command produced.

A command the server does not know, and a command used wrongly, both come
back here with `type` reading `error`: the composer prints the text either
way, and neither is a transport failure.

CommandsResponse.description: The command set the composer completes from.

CommentRequest.description:
`POST /review/comment` — anchor a comment to a line range.

Read into a typed body rather than forwarded as raw JSON, so the session
under review can only ever be the one in the path: a `session_id` in the
body is an unknown field here. The handler copies the fields into a
`ReviewCommentRequest` with the path's session id.

path.description: Absolute, or relative to the session's tracked root.

line_end.description:
1-based, exclusive. Absent means `line_start + 1`, which the daemon
applies — hence `skip_serializing_if`. Sending an explicit `null`
defeats the daemon's `optional_param!` default and is not the same
request.

value.description:
What the effective view holds for the leaf. Always written, `null` when
the view holds nothing there.

ConfigOriginRow.description:
One row of `config.origin`: a leaf, the value the store holds for it, and
where that value came from.

The origin flattens, so `pinned`, `source`, `file` and `line` sit beside
`key` and `value` rather than under a nested object. A settings control
renders a lock from this row, and the file and the line are how it offers a
jump to the line that holds the key.

ConfigResponse.description:
What `GET /api/config` answers.

Three of its fields stay open objects. The effective config, the origin
rows and the control tree are the daemon's vocabulary, declared in Lua and
in the store; a fixed shape here would make this layer a second owner of
them, and a key a newer daemon adds would not reach the browser at all.

remote_shell.description:
Non-loopback terminal/shell access is active (opt-in + API key) —
the terminal panel connects from LAN clients only when this is true.

config.description: The daemon's effective config, whole and unrewritten.

config_root.description:
Where `init.lua` and `settings.json` live, so a lock can offer a jump
to the file that holds a key. Absent when the daemon booted from a
config value rather than a file.

origins.description:
One row per recorded leaf, as `config.origin` gives them. The flat
shape is what a settings control renders a lock from; the effective
config's own `provenance` map is the same fact in the store's enum
shape, and serving both would be two spellings of one answer.

A closed shape, unlike the three fields around it: the daemon builds
every row from one type, so this route reads that type rather than
forwarding an object it cannot describe.

controls.description:
The declared control tree the settings UI renders, as
`config.controls` gives it: `{options, read_only}`. Served here rather
than from a second endpoint because a control and the value it shows
are one screen, and two fetches could disagree about which keys exist.

ConfigSaveReply.description:
What `config.save` answers.

A refusal rides in the answer rather than in an error: refusal is per leaf,
the siblings the caller changed in the same call did save, and `refused`
carries the file and the line a human's config holds the key on.

ok.description: Whether every leaf the caller sent reached the `Settings` layer.

refused.description: The leaves a pin refused, each with the source that holds it.

rejected.description:
The top-level keys that name where the daemon acts, which no save may
write. They are dropped rather than refused, so they are reported apart
from `refused`.

context_strategy.description:
The strategy's string spelling, or `null` where the session carries no
choice of its own.

kilns.description:
The session's kiln set by registry NAME — flat, no member privileged.
Empty or omitted is a literal empty set, NOT a request for a default:
it creates a session with no corpus attached. The daemon stopped
substituting its data root here because that root is the parent of the
sessions store, so "default" quietly put every transcript in scope.

endpoint.description: Custom endpoint URL (optional, for self-hosted models)

agent_name.description: ACP agent profile name (e.g. "claude", "opencode"); required when agent_type == "acp"

agent_card.description: Internal-agent card name; never resolved in the web layer.

isolation.description:
Isolation override: absent → resolve normally; `false` → no container
even if the project has one; `true`, a profile name or an environment
object → override. Forwarded to the daemon untouched — the vocabulary
belongs to the plugin that resolves it, and an unknown profile comes
back as `-32602`, which `daemon_err` turns into a 422.

oneOf.description: The expected text is not in the file. It moved on, or was never there.
The text appears more than once and the edit named no occurrence.
`occurrence` named a match the file does not have.
Two edits in one batch cover the same lines.
`expect` was empty, which would match everywhere and nowhere.

EditRefusal.description: Why one edit could not be applied. The index is the caller's edit index.

command.description: The command line, with or without its leading slash.

FileEntryRow.description: One entry of a kiln's file listing.

name.description: The file stem, or the whole path when the stem is not UTF-8.

is_dir.description:
Always `false`: this listing walks the note index, which holds files.
The key stays because the file tree reads one entry type for every
source, and `GET /api/fs/list` does report directories.

oneOf.description:
A whole write whose base was stale and whose merge left a region the
two sides disagree about. Nothing was written.

current_hash.description: BLAKE3 of the file as it is on disk NOW.

current_content.description:
The disk's text, so the caller can resolve without a second read
that would race the same way.

merged_content.description: The merge's own text, conflicts included.

regions.description: Every cluster the two sides disagree about.

oneOf.description:
A patch the daemon refused. `failed` is empty when the base alone
refused the batch, before any anchor was read.

stale_base.description:
Whether the file moved on since `base_hash` was read. `false` means
the anchors themselves refused.

oneOf.description:
A whole write whose base was stale and which sent no `base_text`, so
there was nothing to merge with. Nothing was written.

FileWriteConflict.description:
What a write answers when it refuses with 409.

Untagged, and the variant order is load-bearing: serde takes the first that
fits. Each arm names a field the others do not have — `regions` for a merge
that could not settle, `failed` for a refused patch, `error` for a bare
refusal — so the three are disjoint and
`a_conflict_reads_back_as_the_arm_that_was_sent` asserts each direction.

FileWriteResponse.description:
What a write answers when it lands.

One type for `PUT` and `PATCH`, because the daemon builds one object for
both: a patch never merges, so it writes no `merged` key, and a whole
write always does.

ok.description:
Always `true` here. A `false` carries a 409 and one of the
[`FileWriteConflict`] shapes instead.

merged.description:
Whether the caller's base was stale and its text was merged with the
disk. Absent on a `PATCH`, which never merges.

content.description:
What was written, present only when `merged` is `true`. The caller
holds it nowhere else: its own text is not what landed.

content_hash.description:
BLAKE3 of what was written, so the caller needs no second read to
learn the hash its next write must name.

FocusedNoteRow.description: The note the panel is about.

path.description: As the index holds it: kiln-relative in normal operation.

abs_path.description:
The same note joined onto the kiln root, which is what
`GET /api/kiln/file` takes.

title.description: The empty string when the index holds no title. Never `null`.

FsEntry.description:
One directory entry in an `fs.list_dir` response.

Wire keys (`name`/`rel_path`/`is_dir`/`size`/`modified`/`status`) are
byte-identical to the TypeScript `FsEntry`. `status` is a Phase-1 decoration
seam and is always `None`.

modified.description:
Unix epoch seconds, or `null` when the platform cannot report it.
Always written.

status.description:
The git/diff decoration seam. Always `null` today, and deliberately
open: whatever fills it will not be a string.

FsEvent.description:
A filesystem change delivered to the browser.

Serializes with an internal `type` tag whose values are `changed` /
`deleted` / `moved` (e.g. `{"type":"changed","path":"/abs","kind":"modified"}`).
The SSE `event:` name is separate — see [`FsEvent::event_name`].

FsListing.description:
One directory level, plus whether the cap cut it short.

Both keys are part of the cross-language contract (TypeScript `FsListing`).
The response used to be a bare array, which had nowhere to say "there is
more" — so a capped listing would have been indistinguishable from a complete
one, which is worse than the slow response it replaces.

FsMkdirResponse.description:
What `POST /api/fs/mkdir` answers.

The route's own shape, not the daemon's: `fs_mkdir` reports success as
`()`, so there is no daemon body to forward.

created.description: Always true. A refusal is an error status, not a `false`.

root.description: Absolute path of the root both ends sit inside.

kind.description: Which allowlist the daemon checks `root` against.

from_rel.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the entry to move.

FsMoveReply.description:
What `fs.move` answers.

The two link-report keys are absent for a move the link index does not
watch — a directory, an asset, a project file — which is the shape the
browser already reads. They were written as a `json!` literal beside the
handler, where nothing held them to the reply the web route promises.

moved.description: Always true. A move that did not happen is an error, not a `false`.

rewritten_sources.description:
Sources whose inbound links were rewritten. Kiln note and canvas moves
only. Absent, never null, for a move with nothing to report.

skipped.description:
Inbound links left as they were, with the reason for each. Absent,
never null, for a move with nothing to report.

root.description: Absolute path of the root the entry sits inside.

kind.description: Which allowlist the daemon checks `root` against.

rel_path.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the entry.

FsRootKind.description:
The two roots a mutation may name, and the allowlist each one selects.

This describes the wire; the field that carries it stays a `String` so that
an unknown kind is refused by the daemon, in the daemon's own sentence,
rather than by a body rejection that says only "unknown variant".
`every_root_kind_is_one_the_daemon_admits` walks an exhaustive match, so a
third kind cannot reach the document without a decision about it.

trashed.description: Always true. A refusal is an error, not a `false`.

trash_path.description: Where the entry now sits, RELATIVE to the root it was trashed from.

GraphLinkRow.description: One edge of the note-link graph.

source.description: The linking note's path. Always a `path` in `notes`.

target.description:
The linked note's path when `resolved`; otherwise the target as it was
written, which names no note.

resolved.description: Whether `target` resolves to a note the caller can see.

GraphNoteRow.description: One node of the note-link graph.

path.description: Kiln-relative, and the value a resolved link's `target` joins against.

title.description: Never empty: the daemon falls back to the file stem.

GrepHit.description:
A single content-search hit.

`match_start`/`match_end` are **character** offsets into `text` (post-trim),
suitable for `<mark>` highlighting in the web UI. Only the first match on a
line is reported. Wire keys (`path`/`rel_path`/`line`/`text`/`match_start`/
`match_end`) are the `search_grep` RPC + `POST /api/search/grep` contract.

path.description: Absolute path to the matched file.

rel_path.description: Path relative to the search's `rel_base` (forward-slash separators).

text.description:
The matched line, trimmed of surrounding whitespace and capped at
[`GREP_SNIPPET_CAP`] characters.

match_start.description: Character offset of the first match's start within `text`.

match_end.description: Character offset of the first match's end within `text`.

GrepSearchRequest.description:
Request for `search_grep` (ripgrep-style content search).

`root` must resolve inside a registered project or open kiln — the daemon
rejects anything else. `glob` filters by file name (e.g. `*.md`); `None`
searches all files.

regex.description:
Compile `query` as a regex (Rust regex syntax) instead of matching it
as a literal substring.

limit.description: The handler still clamps this to `1..=GREP_MAX_LIMIT`.

case_insensitive.description: Defaults to `true`, which is what the handler's `optional_param!` did.

GrepSearchResponse.description:
Result of a `search_grep` call: the hits plus whether they were capped at
the requested limit. Matches the `POST /api/search/grep` response body.

url.description: Plugin URL (e.g. "user/repo" or full git URL).

InteractionRespondResponse.description: The answer this route gives when the daemon took the response.

ok.description: Always `true`. A refusal is an error status, not a `false`.

response.description:
The answer, in the kind-tagged shape `InteractionResponse` takes.

Open, because the vocabulary belongs to the daemon's interaction types
and an unreadable answer must come back as this route's 400 naming the
deserialiser's own complaint, not as axum's plain-text rejection.

content_hash.description:
BLAKE3 of the bytes just read, so a later write can say whether the
file moved on. NOT the index's hash, which lags a save.

KilnFilesResponse.description:
What `GET /api/kiln/files` and `GET /api/kiln/notes` both answer.

One type for two routes because they answer the same projection of the same
listing. The key is `files` on both, including on the one named for notes.

KilnRequest.description:
The body of `POST /connect_kiln` and `POST /disconnect_kiln`.

Named without the `Session` prefix its siblings drop, because the daemon's
RPC client declares a `SessionKilnRequest` that is a different shape going
the other way: that one is `Serialize` and carries `session_id`, this one is
`Deserialize` and takes the id from the URL path.

kiln.description:
The kiln's registry NAME, validated on the way in — a browser that sent
a path gets a 422 rather than a session attached to a directory the
registration floor never saw.

KilnRow.description:
One kiln, as the daemon's `kiln.list` reports it.

Every key is written on every row, including the two an older reader
treated as optional, so this reply carries no absent-versus-false ambiguity.

path.description: Where the kiln lives. This is the one listing whose job is to say so.

name.description:
The REGISTRY key — the name every other API call answers to. An open
directory that no entry names carries the empty string, never `null`.

registered.description:
Whether the registry answers for this directory, and therefore whether
`name` is a name an attach accepts. A row with `false` must not be
offered in a picker.

open.description:
Whether the daemon holds the kiln open right now. A closed row is not a
dead one: the first request that addresses a kiln opens it.

last_access_secs_ago.description:
Seconds since the daemon last touched the kiln, or `null` when it holds
it closed. Always written, so `required` rather than optional.

KnobRow.description:
One setting and whether this session can change it.

Mirrors `crucible_core::types::KnobDescriptor`, for the reason
[`ReviewPolicyRow`] gives.

supported.description:
`false` means the control should not be offered: the daemon refuses
the call.

LayoutWriteResponse.description:
What a layout write answers.

`POST` and `DELETE /api/layout` answer the same object, because both say
only that the file on disk now reflects the request. One type keeps them
from separating.

ok.description: Always true. A failed write is an error status, not a `false`.

allOf.description:
The source that owns the leaf, with its file and line when it has
them.

pinned.description:
Whether a boot-restored layer holds this leaf, so `config.save`
refuses it.

LeafOrigin.description:
Where one leaf came from, and whether `config.save` would refuse it.

The row `config.origin` answers with. `pinned` is the refusal rule itself,
reported per leaf, and the [`SourceOrigin`] beside it is the pin that
refuses — the same one the refusal carries. See [`crate::config::ConfigStore::origin`]
for why the pin, and not the last writer, names the file here.

LineRangeRow.description: A half-open range of 1-based line numbers: `end` is one past the last line.

end.description: One past the last line, 1-based, exclusive.

port.description: The SSE port, or `null` under stdio. Always written.

kiln_path.description: The kiln path the server serves.

finished.description:
Whether the server task has already finished, which is how a crashed
server reads while the manager still calls itself running.

oneOf.description:
A server is serving a kiln. Listed first so a payload that carries the
running keys never reads as the stopped arm, which ignores them.
No server is running.

McpStatus.description:
What `mcp.status` answers: the server is up, or it is not.

Untagged, because the two arms are told apart by `running` and the wire
has always spelled them that way. The stopped arm carries `running` ALONE:
a stopped server has no transport, no port and no kiln, and writing those
keys as null would say it has them and they are empty.

MergeRegion.description:
A cluster both sides changed differently.

The lines are 1-based and the end is exclusive, the convention
`crate::session::types::review::LineRange` uses, and they point into the
MERGED text, so a reader can show the region without diffing again.

start_line.description: First line of the region in the merged text, 1-based, inclusive.

end_line.description:
One past the last line of the region in the merged text, exclusive.
Equal to `start_line` when our side deleted the cluster.

base.description: The cluster as the base held it.

ours.description: The cluster as our side wrote it. This is what the merged text holds.

theirs.description: The cluster as their side wrote it.

mode.description: The session's mode id. `null` is the normal mode.

ModeRow.description:
One mode a session may enter.

Mirrors `crucible_core::types::mode::ModeDescriptor` field for field, for
the reason [`ReviewPolicyRow`] gives.

name.description: The label to draw.

icon.description: An emoji or an icon name.

review_policy.description:
The review this mode asks for, already degraded to what this session's
agent can enforce.

ModelsResponse.description:
Response for model listings — the session-scoped `list_models` and the
session-less `list_all_models` return the same `{ models: [...] }` shape.

NoteMetadataRow.description: One note, with the metadata a client filters and sorts on.

name.description: The file stem, or the whole path when the stem is not UTF-8.

path.description:
RELATIVE to the kiln root. A path-taking endpoint needs it joined onto
the root first.

title.description: The note's own title, or `null` when it declares none. Always written.

updated_at.description:
ISO-8601, or `null` for a note the index has no timestamp for. Always
written.

properties.description:
The note's own frontmatter, filtered daemon-side to what the author
wrote. Open by design: a note may carry any key, and validating the
values here would refuse frontmatter this layer has no business judging.

NoteResponse.description:
One note, as `get_note_by_name` reports it.

The daemon sends `links_to` and `wikilinks` for the same links: the web
reader pins `links_to`, and the RPC client's own DTO reads `wikilinks`.
Both stay on the wire, so both are named here.

title.description:
The note's title. The daemon writes the empty string when it has none;
this is never `null`.

links_to.description: Every wikilink target in the note, as written.

wikilinks.description: The same targets, one object each.

content_hash.description:
BLAKE3 of the note's content as the INDEX holds it. The file watcher
writes it asynchronously, so it lags a save; `GET /api/kiln/file`
answers the hash of the bytes on disk.

name.description:
The file name written, `.md` included — which is not always the `name`
that was asked for.

title.description: The first heading of the content, or its first line.

updated_at.description: When this route wrote it, not when the index noticed.

OkResponse.description: Standard acknowledgment response for successful mutations.

OptionRequest.description:
One read, write, or button press against a plugin's settings tree.

A single endpoint because the three differ only in which Lua callback they
reach — the same reason the daemon handler is one function. `value` is
present for a set and ignored otherwise.

path.description: The path through the settings tree to the option.

value.description: The new value, for a `set`. Ignored otherwise.

PatchFileRequest.description: `PATCH /api/kiln/file` — change a few lines, not the whole file.

base_hash.description:
The disk hash the caller last read. Present, it gates: the batch is
refused with 409 and `stale_base: true` when the file moved on, even
when every anchor applies. Absent, the anchors alone decide; the outbox
replay sends no base, because it edits the note's current text.

PendingInteraction.description: One interaction a session is waiting on an answer to.

request_id.description: The identifier an answer must carry back.

request.description:
The request, in the flat shape the SSE path delivers.

Deliberately open: `normalize_interaction` writes one object per
interaction kind — a permission request carries `tokens` and maybe
`diffs`, an ask carries the question's own fields — and the kinds are
the daemon's to add to. `kind` tells the browser which one it has.

PendingInteractionsResponse.description: The interactions every session is waiting on, in one list.

allOf.description:
The source that holds the leaf, with the file and line when it has
them, so the caller can offer a jump to that line.

key.description: The dot-joined leaf path the caller asked to save.

PinnedLeaf.description: One leaf `config.save` refuses, and what pins it.

PluginCommandRow.description:
One executable primitive a plugin declared, and the arguments it takes.

**A deliberate reshape, so it keeps its own struct.** The daemon builds a
row from `crucible_core::traits::tools::ToolDefinition`, but it sends three
of that type's seven fields — `name`, `description` and `parameters` — and
adds three the command registry owns: the declaring `plugin`, the
`hint`, and the declared `effect`. `category`, `returns`, `examples` and
`required_permissions` never reach a client. Re-exporting `ToolDefinition`
would therefore promise four keys the wire does not carry, which is why
this is not one of the types to derive `ToSchema` on in `crucible-core`.

name.description:
Globally unique: the daemon refuses a second plugin claiming a name,
which is why `POST /api/plugins/command` does not route by plugin.

hint.description: The one-line argument hint, or `null`. Always written, so `required`.

parameters.description:
The declared parameters, as the JSON Schema `signature.rs` emits, or
`null` for a command that takes none.

Opaque on purpose, like a publication: the reader turns it into the
controls a dialog draws, and a shape validated here would be one only
today's plugins could send.

oneOf.description: Cloned, and checked out at the pin if one was given.
Already cloned at the expected destination; no work done.
Disabled in config; skipped.

PluginInstallOutcomeRow.description:
`POST /api/plugins` — clone a plugin from a git URL and record it in
the installed manifest (`plugins.installed.json`), the same record
`cru plugin add` writes. The operator's own spec entries live in
`init.lua`, which nothing here edits. Synchronous; can take 10+ seconds.
What the clone did, tagged by `kind`.

Mirrors `crucible_daemon::BootstrapOutcome`, which is what
`server/plugin_install.rs` matches on to write these three objects.
`the_mirrored_vocabularies_stay_closed` fails to compile if a fourth
outcome appears there.

name.description: The installed plugin's name, as the URL resolved it.

installed.description: The clone and the manifest record happened.

loaded.description:
The plugin also activated on the running daemon.

`installed: true` with `loaded: false` is a plugin that reached the disk
and broke on load; `error` says why, and the next boot tries again. A
client must not read `installed` alone as success.

error.description: Why the plugin did not load, or `null`. Always written, so `required`.

watch.description:
A sentence about hot reload. The watcher's list is a boot-time
snapshot, so a plugin installed at runtime works but is not rewatched.

manifest.description:
The installed manifest the entry was written to
(`plugins.installed.json`).

The browser's hand-written type calls this key `plugins_toml`, which the
daemon has not sent since the record moved out of TOML — so today that
field reads `undefined` at run time and nothing said so. A12 renames it.

oneOf.description: The answer to `action: "get"`.
The answer to `action: "set"` and `action: "execute"`.

PluginOptionCallResponse.description:
What `POST /api/plugins/{name}/option` answers.

Untagged, because one endpoint serves three actions: a `get` answers a
value where a `set` and an `execute` answer an acknowledgement.

**The variant order is load-bearing** — the hazard `ResumeSessionResponse`
was fixed for. Serde takes the first variant that fits, so a union whose
first variant also fits the second's bodies reads every one of them as the
wrong thing. These two are disjoint today because neither field has a
default: `{"ok": true}` has no `value` and `{"value": …}` has no `ok`.
`an_option_reply_reads_back_as_the_action_that_sent_it` asserts both
directions, so a `#[serde(default)]` added to either field fails there
rather than on a browser.

value.description:
Whatever the plugin's getter returned, and `null` is an answer.

Opaque: an option's type belongs to the plugin, and the renderer reads
the value against the node that declared it.

PluginOptionsResponse.description:
What `GET /api/plugins/options` answers: one settings tree per plugin.

**A deliberate narrowing to the envelope.** The tree itself stays opaque,
and that is not laziness about a shape nobody wrote down — the nodes are
fully described in `crucible-lua`'s `describe_node`. It is about numbers:
`order`, `min`, `max`, `step` and every entry under `values` reach here as
whatever `lua_to_json` made of the plugin's Lua, so reading one into an
`f64` and writing it back would send `100.0` where the daemon sent `100`.
The browser renders a node generically anyway, so naming the map's keys is
the whole gain a mirrored node type would offer.

PluginReloadResponse.description:
What `POST /api/plugins/{name}/reload` answers: the capabilities the
reloaded spec declares.

name.description: The plugin that was reloaded, echoed.
The plugin that was removed, as the manifest named it.

manifest.description:
The installed manifest the entry left. See
[`PluginInstallResponse::manifest`] for the name the browser still uses.

purged_dir.description: The directory that was deleted, or `null` without `?purge=true`.

purge_error.description: The manifest entry went but deleting the directory failed.

kept_dir.description:
Removed without a purge, and the directory is still there.

It sits in a permanent search path, so the next daemon start discovers
and loads it again. `null` when nothing is left behind, which is the
only case where "removed" means gone.

PluginRow.description:
One discovered plugin, as `plugin.list`'s `plugin_info` rows describe it.

Every discovered plugin, not only the healthy ones: a plugin that failed to
load carries its reason in `last_error`, and dropping it would make "broken"
read as "not installed".

version.description:
`null` when the plugin has no fragment, or its fragment names no
version. The daemon always writes the key, so `required` rather than
optional.

source.description:
Where the plugin came from: `User`, `Runtime`, `EnvPath` or `Builtin`.
A plain string, because the daemon writes `Display` output rather than
a serde spelling.

state.description:
The lifecycle state: `Active`, `Error` or `Disabled`. A plain string
for the same reason as `source`.

last_error.description:
Why the plugin is not `Active`, or `null` for a healthy one. Always
written, so `required`.

dir.description: The absolute directory the plugin was discovered in.

PluginRunCommandResponse.description:
What `POST /api/plugins/command` answers.

The browser's hand-written caller types this as a bare `unknown`, so a
reader had to know to look under `result` without anything saying so. The
envelope is the daemon's (`server/plugins.rs`'s `handle_plugin_run_command`),
and naming it costs the plugin nothing: `result` stays opaque.

name.description: The command that ran, echoed.

result.description:
Whatever the command's Lua `fn` returned.

Opaque, like publications and options: what a command returns is the
plugin's vocabulary, and a shape validated here would be one only
today's plugins could send.

Project.description:
A registered project — a directory the user works on.

Projects group sessions by workspace path and provide metadata
for display in the UI (name, attached kilns, etc.).

path.description: Canonical path to the project root directory

name.description: Human-readable name (from `ProjectConfig.project.name` or dirname)

kilns.description:
Attached kilns (from `ProjectConfig` or auto-discovered .crucible/)

`default` covers a stored project written before the field existed. It
is always WRITTEN, empty or not, so a reader never sees it absent.

last_accessed.description: When this project was last accessed

oneOf.description: SCM/repository information (if detected)

name.description:
The kiln's registry name. A kiln that declares none sends NO `name`
key, so a reader must treat the field as absent rather than null.

path.description: Absolute path of the project root.

ProjectUnregisterResponse.description:
What `POST /api/project/unregister` answers.

The route's own shape: the daemon reports the unregistration as `()`, so
there is no daemon body to forward.

ok.description: Always true. A refusal is an error status, not a `false`.

ProviderRow.description:
One LLM provider the daemon found.

Mirrors `crucible_core::types::ProviderInfo` field for field. It is
declared here rather than re-exported because `crucible-core` takes no
utoipa dependency, and a schema is what puts the fields in the document.

provider_type.description: The backend behind the provider, such as `ollama` or `openai`.

available.description: Whether the provider answered its probe.

reason.description: Why the provider is unavailable, when it is.

is_local.description: Whether the provider runs on this machine.

PublicationChangedEvent.description:
A plugin's published data changed, delivered to the browser.

Carries who published and under which key, never the value — the same
contract the daemon event has, and for the same reason: a publication is
opaque JSON of the plugin's own choosing. The browser refetches through
`GET /api/plugins/publications`.

Projected through a named type rather than passed through as raw `data`,
which is the treatment `SurfaceChangedEvent` already gets: a field the
daemon renames then breaks the browser with nothing on this side to notice.

base_hash.description:
The hash the caller read. Absent keeps the blind overwrite; present
refuses with 409 and the current hash when the file moved on.

The hash the caller read. Absent keeps the blind overwrite; present
refuses with 409 and the current hash when the file moved on.

base_text.description:
The text the caller read, whose hash is `base_hash`. Present, a stale
base is merged against the disk instead of refused: the caller loses
its edit otherwise, and it is the only party that holds the text its
edit was made from. Absent, the refusal stands.

base_hash.description:
The hash the caller read. Absent keeps the blind overwrite; present
refuses with 409 and the current hash when the file moved on.

kiln.description: Absolute path of the kiln to write into. It must be registered.

abs_path.description: Absolute path of the file that was opened.

name.description: The file's display name, as the client recorded it.

opened_at.description: Unix millis of the last open — set server-side on record.

RecentsResponse.description:
What both recents routes answer: the list, newest first.

`GET` and `POST /api/recents` answer the same projection under the same
key, so one type keeps the read and the write from separating.

abs_path.description: Absolute path of the file that was opened.

name.description: The file's display name.

RejectedRefDto.description:
A reference the read path refused, as the browser receives it.

Web-owned on purpose, and NOT a re-export of
[`crucible_core::canvas::containment::RejectedRef`]. The core type carries
`reference` — the offending path itself — and this reply deliberately drops
it: a client that never learns the path cannot ask for it, which is what
makes redaction an enforcement rather than a warning. The node id is
`nodeId` here because the canvas format is camelCase throughout, and the
browser reads it beside `fromNode` and `toNode`.

nodeId.description: Id of the node holding the bad reference.

reason.description:
Why it was refused, as a sentence to show the reader.

A rendered [`RefError`], not a token. The browser prints it; nothing
branches on it, and `the_refusal_reasons_stay_whole_sentences` pins
every variant's wording so a reworded error is a visible change rather
than a silent one.

RepositoryInfo.description: Information about the git repository containing this project.

root.description: Path to the repository root (where .git is, or main repo for worktrees)

is_worktree.description:
Whether this project is in a git worktree (not the main checkout).
Always written, so `required` rather than optional.

main_repo_git_dir.description: For worktrees: path to the main repository's .git directory

ResolvedNoteResponse.description:
Where a wikilink target landed.

`absolutePath` is camelCase while every sibling reply is snake_case: the
browser has read that spelling since before this route was typed, and
renaming it would break the editor's open-a-link path for no gain.

path.description: Relative to the root that was walked.

absolutePath.description: The absolute path, which is what an editor opens.

title.description: The file stem, or `null` when the path has none. Always written.

oneOf.description: The session came back from the store.
The session was resident and merely paused.

ResumeSessionResponse.description:
What `POST /api/session/{id}/resume` answers, which depends on the path
that resumed the session.

The warm path answers the state change. The cold path reloads the session
from the store and answers its history, because that call is also what
`GET /api/session/{id}/history` serves.

**`Restored` must stay first.** The daemon sends no tag, so the variants
are told apart by their fields, and `Live`'s required fields
(`session_id`, `state`) are a subset of `Restored`'s. An untagged enum
takes the first variant that fits, so with the order reversed every
restored history would read back as a bare state change and every event
would be dropped without an error. `a_restored_payload_does_not_read_as_a_live_one`
holds the order.

`deny_unknown_fields` would be the other way to separate them, and it is
not used here: these are daemon replies, and refusing a field a newer
daemon added would turn an extension into a 502 on three healthy routes.

comment.description:
The comment as it was stored, with the id and the time the daemon
minted.

ReviewCommentRow.description: One review comment, anchored to a line range rather than to a hunk.

base_tree.description:
The tree the range is anchored in. A range that no longer projects
forward from it is outdated.

created_at.description:
When the comment was written, RFC 3339.

A string rather than a date type: the daemon's spelling reaches the
browser unchanged, and a parse and a reformat here could only lose
precision the daemon sent.

ReviewFailureRow.description: One hunk a bulk decision refused, with the daemon's reason.

ReviewGateRow.description: A turn parked on the review gate, waiting for a human.

path.description:
The first target still unreviewed — what a human must answer to release
the turn.

ReviewHunkRow.description:
One hunk of the composed diff, the unit a decision applies to.

There is no `external` field, here or on the wire: a hunk is external when
`tool_call_ids` is empty, which is what `isExternal` reads in the browser.

id.description: Content-derived, and the only handle a decision names.

root.description: The repository top level this hunk belongs to.

base_range.description: The lines this hunk replaces, in base coordinates.

current_range.description: The lines it occupies now, in worktree coordinates.

before_content.description: The base-side text. Empty for a pure insertion.

after_content.description: The current-side text. Empty for a pure deletion.

tool_call_ids.description: The tool calls whose writes survive into this hunk, in ledger order.

reapplied.description:
The agent applied a change the user had rejected. The state comes back
`unreviewed`; this is the history that makes the grind visible.

scope.description:
The scope the answer describes, echoed. A client that switched scope
while a listing was in flight reads it to drop the stale answer.

degraded.description:
Only the roots that are broken. An empty array is the common case; a
non-empty one means the gate holds writes that no reviewing releases.

oneOf.description:
What this session's turn is parked on, or `null`.

Always written, and `required` in the document for that reason: a
client has to be able to tell "not blocked" from "this daemon does not
report it", and an optional key collapses the two.

ReviewIntegrityRow.description:
What the journal could not be read back as.

Separate from the degraded roots because the worst losses are the ones with
no root to name: a journal that will not read at all leaves `degraded`
empty while the gate holds every write in the session.

ReviewPolicyRow.description:
How much review a mode asks for before the agent writes.

Mirrors `crucible_core::types::mode::ReviewPolicy`, which carries no
schema: `crucible-core` takes no utoipa dependency, and a client that
renders a mode chip has to know the three values it can read.

roots.description:
Every tracked root and what the rebase could do for it. A root that
still carries a reason was not recovered.

ReviewRootRow.description: Whether the ledger can still account for one tracked root.

degraded.description:
Why this root's attribution cannot be trusted. `null` is intact, and
the string is shown to the user as the daemon wrote it. The key is
always written, so `required` rather than optional.

ReviewScopeRow.description:
Which hunks a listing covers, as `crucible_core::session::ReviewScope`
spells it on the wire.

Web-owned because a schema is what puts the two values in the document, and
`crucible-core` takes no `utoipa` dependency. [`From`] converts it to the
core type, so a variant added there fails to compile here rather than
reaching the daemon as a scope this crate silently narrowed.

oneOf.description:
The session's base is untrustworthy, so every root blocks — including
ones the ledger may no longer know it tracked.
One root's attribution is incomplete. Only writes under it block.
A lost decision or comment. The queue is poorer, not wrong.

ReviewSkipKindRow.description: What a skipped journal record costs.

ReviewSkipRow.description: One journal record the daemon could not read back.

line.description: The 1-based line in `review.jsonl`, so an operator can find it.

ReviewStateRow.description: One user decision about one hunk.

ReviewStatesResponse.description:
What `POST /api/session/{id}/review/states` answers.

A refused hunk is part of the answer rather than an error status: the ids
in `applied` are on disk whatever happened to the rest, and a client told
only "failed" would have to re-list to learn which were which.

applied.description: The ids that applied, in the order the request sent them.

ReviewUndoRejectResponse.description:
What `POST /api/session/{id}/review/undo-reject` answers.

The same report as a bulk decision, minus the state: an undo restores
whatever the batch rejected. An empty stack answers two empty lists.

SaveRequest.description:
The values one save carries, in the shape `config.save` takes.

The keys are config leaf paths and the values are whatever those leaves
hold, so the map stays open: which leaves exist is the daemon's answer.

path.description: Absolute path of the freshly cloned repository.

SemanticSearchRequest.description:
`POST /api/search/semantic` — text semantic search over a kiln's notes.
Embeds the query with the kiln's embedding provider, then cosine-scans the
embeddings in the kiln's SQLite store. Two daemon RPCs (`embed.query` +
`search_vectors`) mirror the CLI's `run_semantic_search`. The daemon
answers with one row per block, best first. The panel lists notes, so
this route keeps one row per note: its best block, with `block` and
`snippet` when the kiln has block rows. Each hit's `document_id` is the
kiln-relative note path; `path` is the absolute path for the editor to
open. Requires an embedding provider (else `embed.query` fails) AND
processed notes (no embeddings yields no hits).

kiln.description: Absolute path of the kiln to search.

SemanticSearchRow.description: One note hit, with the block that earned it.

document_id.description:
The note's kiln-relative path. The same value as `rel_path`; both stay
because the browser reads both.

rel_path.description: The note's kiln-relative path, for display.

path.description: The absolute path, which is what an editor opens.

oneOf.description:
The note's best block, or `null` when the kiln has no block rows.
Always written.

snippet.description: The block's text, or `null` when there is none. Always written.

SendMessageResponse.description:
The identifier the daemon minted for the turn this request started.

One key, because the browser correlates the SSE events that follow with it
and needs nothing else to do so.

SessionAgentRow.description:
The agent record `session.get` nests inside a session.

Two fields are named because a client reads them: `model`, which
`session.list` sends flat as `agent_model`, and `mode`. Every other field
of the daemon's record rides in `rest`, so this projection narrows what the
document describes without dropping anything from the reply.

model.description: The model this session's agent runs.

mode.description: The session mode id. Absent when the session is in the normal mode.

additionalProperties.description: Every other field of the daemon's agent record, carried verbatim.

SessionHistoryEvent.description:
One persisted session event, as `session.resume_from_storage` replays it.

The same envelope the SSE stream carries, but this route replays whatever
the transcript holds — including an event name a newer daemon minted — so
`data` stays untyped here rather than narrowing to [`crate::events::ChatEvent`].

event.description: The event name, such as `user_message` or `text_delta`.

data.description: The event payload. Its shape follows `event`.

history.description: The page of events the query asked for.

total_events.description: How many events the whole transcript holds, for paging.

knobs.description:
Every knob Crucible has, answered for. A client that finds an id
missing is talking to an older daemon.

previous_state.description: The state the session left. `session.end` does not send it.

state.description: The state the session is in now.

kilns.description: The session's kilns. Only `session.end` sends them.

total.description: How many sessions the reply carries.

current_mode_id.description: The mode the session is in. Always one of `modes`.

modes.description: Every mode the session may switch to, in declaration order.

SessionRow.description:
One session, as every session route answers it.

Three daemon methods build three different objects for one entity.
`session.create` sends no `started_at` and no `title`. `session.get` nests
the model under `agent` and sends no `event_count`, `last_activity` or
`archived`. `session.list` sends the model flat and sends all three. This
declares the union once, so a client reads one type instead of reconciling
three. The divergence is a daemon bug (`server/session/list.rs:155` against
`:302`); this route does not fix it.

A field that one shape omits and another sends as `null` carries
`Option<Option<T>>`. The outer level is "the daemon wrote no key", the
inner one is "the key is null". Both spellings then reach the browser as
the daemon wrote them, which is what keeps this projection lossless.

session_id.description: The session id. The wire name is `session_id`, never `id`.

type.description: The session type prefix, such as `chat`.

kilns.description: Every kiln the session can query, by registry name.

workspace.description: The session's working directory. `null` is a session with no workspace.

state.description: The session state, such as `active` or `paused`.

started_at.description: When the session started. `session.create` does not send it.

title.description: The session title. `session.create` does not send it.

agent_model.description:
The resolved model. `session.get` does not send it; read `agent.model`
there.

last_activity.description: The last event's time. Only `session.list` sends it.

event_count.description: How many events the transcript holds. Only `session.list` sends it.

archived.description: Whether the session is archived. Only `session.list` sends it.

parent_session_id.description: The parent of a delegated session. `session.create` does not send it.

continued_from.description: The session this one continues. Only `session.get` sends it.

oneOf.description: The session's agent record. Only `session.get` sends it.

recording_mode.description:
How the session records its transcript. `session.get` sends it only
when the session has a recording mode.

SessionScopeResponse.description: The session scope that a kiln or workspace mutation echoes.

kilns.description: Every kiln the session can query, by registry name.

workspace.description: The session's working directory. `null` is a session with no workspace.

SessionSearchMatch.description:
One transcript line that matched a session search.

Not a session: the daemon answers the line it matched on, so a caller that
wants the session reads `session_id` and asks for it.

line.description:
The 1-based line of the transcript. `0` marks a title match on a
session whose transcript has not reached disk yet.

context.description: The matched line, truncated to 100 characters.

total.description: How many matches the reply carries.

note.description:
Why the search looked at nothing, when it looked at nothing.

The daemon writes it for a search with no kiln scope
(`server/session/list.rs:206`), and only then. An unscoped search is
the one case where an empty result is not a statement about the
corpus, so the sentence has to reach the caller.

status.description:
Every slot the session has, sorted by key. A session that published
nothing answers an empty list.

SessionStatusSlot.description:
One keyed status slot a plugin published for a session.

`key`, `plugin` and `level` stay plain strings rather than unions on
purpose. The moment a client enumerates them, a new plugin needs a client
change to be visible at all, which is the thing this channel exists to
avoid.

key.description: What the slot is about. The plugin chooses it.

level.description: How loud the line is, such as `info` or `warn`.

SetStateRequest.description: `POST /review/state` — accept, reject, or requeue one hunk.

state.description:
Forwarded unvalidated: the daemon owns the state vocabulary and answers
`INVALID_PARAMS` for anything outside it. A copy of the enum here could
only ever refuse a state the daemon had newly learned.

SetStatesRequest.description:
`POST /review/states` — one decision over several hunks, in order.

The ids reach the daemon in the order the caller gave them, because the
daemon applies them in that order and a reject reverts files as it goes.
`state` is forwarded unvalidated for the same reason as on
[`SetStateRequest`].

workspace.description: Omitted/null → detach: the session is then left with no workspace.

SkillDetail.description: What `skills.get` answers: one skill, with the body a summary omits.

scope.description: The discovery scope the skill came from, as `SkillScope` spells it.

source_path.description: Where the skill file sits on disk.

agent.description: The agent the skill declares, when it declares one. Always written.

license.description: The licence the skill declares, when it declares one. Always written.

body.description: The skill's Markdown body, without its frontmatter.

SkillSummary.description:
One skill in a `skills.list` or `skills.search` answer.

The two RPCs answer the same row, because a list and a search are the same
question asked of two different sets. A second row type here would let one
of them grow a field the other cannot report.

name.description: The skill's name, which is also the key `skills.get` takes.

scope.description: The discovery scope the skill came from, as `SkillScope` spells it.

shadowed_count.description: How many same-named skills this one shadows.

SkipReason.description:
Why one inbound reference was left as it was.

A closed set, because the browser prints a sentence per reason. It was four
string literals spelled in five places, so a fifth reason could reach a
client whose reader has no arm for it. `every_skip_reason_reaches_the_wire`
(`crucible-web`) walks an exhaustive match, so a new variant fails to
compile until somebody decides what the client says about it.

SkippedRef.description: One inbound reference that was intentionally left untouched.

SlashCommand.description: One slash command, as both the `/help` text and the web autocomplete see it.

name.description: Bare name, no leading slash.

args.description: Argument placeholder shown in help/completion, empty when nullary.

SourceOrigin.description:
Where one leaf came from, in the shape the wire uses.

One projection serves two callers: `config.origin` answers with it, and a
`config.save` refusal names the pin with it. Two projections would let the
refusal name a file the origin does not.
`Deserialize` as well as `Serialize`: `config.save`'s refusal travels back
over the RPC into a typed reply, and a `&'static str` cannot be read from a
document. The value is still [`ConfigSource::short`]'s, written once.

source.description: The one-word source name, as [`ConfigSource::short`] gives it.

file.description: The file the source names, when it names one.

line.description: The line inside `file`, when the source recorded one.

SurfaceChangedEvent.description:
A surface changed, delivered to the browser.

Carries the identity and the new version, never the rows — the same contract
the daemon event has, and for the same reason: a surface is unbounded where an
event is not, and two clients want it at different moments. The browser
refetches through `GET /api/surfaces`.

withdrawn.description:
The surface is gone, so the browser drops it instead of refetching.

Passed through rather than re-derived. The daemon knew this when it
dropped the entry, and a browser that had to ask `GET /api/surfaces`
to find out would pay a round trip for a fact the event already held.

SurfaceLineRow.description:
One line of a surface.

Named for a line rather than for a row, because the daemon calls both the
panel and its entries a row and this file needs to name them apart. The
wire key stays `rows`.

id.description:
Stable identity, chosen by the plugin. What an action names later, and
what a client keys a selection on across a re-push.

detail.description:
Secondary text, or `null`. The daemon always writes the key, so
`required` rather than optional.

oneOf.description:
Status, or `null` for a line that has none. `null` is "no status",
never "unknown". Always written, so `required`.

SurfaceMarkRow.description:
A row's status, mirroring [`crucible_lua::Mark`].

Stated semantically, so each client picks its own glyph. Closed for the same
reason [`SurfaceShapeRow`] is closed.

SurfaceRow.description: One declared surface, as `surface.list` reports it.

plugin.description: The plugin that declared it, so a stale surface can be attributed.

name.description: The plugin's own name for it. Stable across a reload.

session.description:
The session this surface is about, or `null` when it is about the
plugin. Always written, so `required`.

version.description:
Bumped on every row change, so a client redraws on a change it sees
rather than on a timer.

SurfaceShapeRow.description:
What a client draws, mirroring [`crucible_lua::Shape`].

A closed set here, and not the open string the browser's hand-written type
declares, because the daemon cannot send anything else: `Shape::parse`
refuses an unknown name when the plugin declares the surface, so a spelling
outside this list never reaches a reply. `the_mirrored_vocabularies_stay_closed`
holds the two lists together — a variant added in `crucible-lua` fails that
test rather than reaching the browser as a shape no renderer knows.

UnlinkedMentionRow.description:
A plain-text mention of another note inside the focused note — a candidate
for one-click link insertion, mirroring the daemon's `LinkSuggestion`.

mention.description: The text as it appears, original casing kept.

target.description: The note name it would link to.

offset.description: Byte offset of the mention in the note's content.

kiln.description: Absolute path of the kiln to search.

vector.description: The query vector, already embedded by the caller.

VectorSearchRow.description: One block hit, as `search_vectors` ranked it.

oneOf.description:
Where in the note the hit sits, or `null` when the hit names the whole
note. Always written, so `null` reads as "the whole note" and never as
"unknown".

WebhookReceiveReply.description:
What `webhook.receive` answers.

Acceptance only: the delivery became a `webhook:received` event, and
whether a plugin was listening is not this answer's business. Every refusal
is an HTTP error at the ingress route, which never reaches this RPC.

WriteErrorRow.description: The error envelope a bare stale-base refusal carries.

code.description: The HTTP status, repeated in the body.
